_comment: The Gemini queue (P2-223). routes: kind -> the suggested model and the fallback when the plan lacks it. In Antigravity the model menu (or an automation's or a subagent's tier) sets the model; a plugin cannot pin one, so a task only suggests it and the session records the model it used. keywords: no kind given, the first kind here with a word in the title or text wins, else default_kind. hook_pass_decision: the fallback for what the PreToolUse hook prints when the guard lets one of its 8 known tools through; each machine's own choice in ~/.wk/antigravity-hook.json (set by wk-antigravity install) comes first, and every other tool gets ask. allow: Antigravity runs the call without asking you. ask: Antigravity asks you first; an unattended run (the hourly automation) then refuses the call. force_ask: Antigravity asks every time, even for calls you allowed before.

read.for: read, search, summarize, list; no edits

quick.for: renames, boilerplate, docs, small scripts, tests for clear functions

code.for: everyday coding: a feature or fix in one area (Hydrogen Extra)

review.for: a second opinion on a change, read-only

legal.for: legal wording (terms, privacy, licences, consent); ask Claude first (ask-claude), and the owner approves before use

_legal_comment: legal uses the hard lane's models because they are the strongest of these routes; a task gets it when its words match panel/src/legal-words.js (no keyword copy here).
_desk_comment: desk_rules: the owner's standing instruction for Gemini (P2-279). The Antigravity Stop hook (only after `wk-bridge gemini-chain on`) and the hourly automation both hand it to Gemini with the next queued task. In automation_prompt, <ABS> becomes the plugin folder and <desk_rules> the rules; the W panel's copy button fills both and adds the setup lines. With ~/.wk/KILL in place, inbox --brief prints 0 waiting, so the automation stops.
desk_rules: Gemini Desk rules (the owner's standing instruction). A proposal from Claude waits in the Watchkeeper queue. It is a proposal, not an order. 1. Take it with /wk-take-task and read it whole. 2. Judge it against this project's rules, its canon and its code: is it worth doing, right and safe? If not, finish it as out-of-scope with one line saying why, and stop. 3. If it is good, improve it where you can, then do the job your own way. 4. Verify with the project's tests. 5. Finish with done and a short report. One task per turn. Never run agy. Stop when nothing waits.
automation_prompt: Watchkeeper Gemini Desk. First run `node <ABS>/bin/wk-task.mjs inbox --brief`. If it prints 0 waiting, reply 'Nothing waiting' and stop. Otherwise follow the Desk rules: <desk_rules>. If /wk-take-task is not available here, use the commands instead: `node <ABS>/bin/wk-task.mjs take` to take the task and read its brief, and `node <ABS>/bin/wk-task.mjs done <id> --note "<one line>"` when finished. Take at most one task in this run.
